faculty.title: Into the Forest with Bonbibi: Tales of Fear, Faith, and Ecology
faculty.author: Dr. Monalisa Bhattacharjee
faculty.overview: A reading of the Bonbibi legend of the Sundarbans as a living cultural framework for coexistence, showing how stories, faith and everyday practice shape ecological awareness alongside science and policy.
faculty.pull: Coexistence does not necessarily mean the absence of conflict, but rather the continuous negotiation of shared spaces, risks, and responsibilities.
text: The Sundarbans, a vast mangrove ecosystem shared by India and Bangladesh, represents a complex relationship between human livelihoods, non-human life, and environmental uncertainty. For communities living along its tidal rivers and forest margins, nature is not merely a physical environment or an economic resource; it is also a cultural and spiritual presence. Among the narratives that shape this relationship, the story of Bonbibi, the guardian of the forest, occupies a significant place in the cultural ecology of the Sundarbans.

Bonbibi is revered by many Hindu and Muslim communities in the region, reflecting a shared tradition that transcends religious boundaries. Her narrative, preserved in the Bonbibi Johuranama, centres on the relationship between humans and the forest, particularly through the figures of Bonbibi, Dokkhin Rai, and Dukhe. Dokkhin Rai, often associated with the tiger, represents the potentially dangerous power of the forest, while Bonbibi offers protection to those who enter it. The story of Dukhe, a vulnerable boy threatened by Dokkhin Rai, highlights the precariousness of human existence in an ecosystem where survival depends on negotiating the boundaries between human needs and non-human forces.

From an ecological perspective, the Bonbibi narrative offers an alternative to the assumption that nature exists primarily for human exploitation. The forest is represented as a domain with its own power, limits, and inhabitants. People who enter it for honey, fish, or other resources must recognise that they are entering a space shared with other living beings.

The narrative can therefore be interpreted as encouraging restraint, respect, and an awareness of human vulnerability. Although it is not a formal conservation code, its moral framework provides a culturally grounded way of thinking about coexistence and the responsible use of natural resources. The story also complicates conventional understandings of human–animal relationships. The tiger is not simply a biological species or an enemy of human livelihood; it occupies a significant position in the cultural imagination of the Sundarbans. Its association with Dokkhin Rai reflects the danger that forest-dependent communities may encounter, while also acknowledging the power of non-human life. This tension reveals an important ecological reality: coexistence does not necessarily mean the absence of conflict, but rather the continuous negotiation of shared spaces, risks, and responsibilities.

In the end, the Bonbibi tradition demonstrates that ecological relationships are formed not only by science and policy but also by stories, beliefs, and everyday cultural practices. It provides a rich lens for understanding how people locate themselves in a more-than-human world and how place-based knowledge can support biocultural resilience. Studying the narrative as a living cultural resource for coexistence can help researchers and practitioners explore how local tales foster ecological awareness and how they might inform more inclusive, community-rooted approaches to conservation and climate adaptation in the Sundarbans, approaches that recognise both the power of the forest and the dignity of those who share it.

articles.title: Beyond Disposal: The Future of Waste
articles.author: Sneha Sahu
articles.overview: How plastic-heavy lifestyles fill our landfills, and how segregation, recycling and smarter choices can turn waste into value.
text: Every used wrapper, thrown-away meal and old electric appliance has the history after getting tossed form the owner’s hands. However, for the most of them, this story ends as they are thrown away on the dustbin. Still, if the overproduction of waste and its specific storages and disposal methods threaten the human existence, it should be changed.

Currently, the solid waste management in modern society is mainly influenced by the increasing number of products wrapped in plastic and the growing tendency to buy more goods online. As such, up-to-date lifestyle brings the changes in people’s habits and behaviors, increased usage of lightweight plastic packaging resulting in more waste than ever. Specifically, careless disposal of trash and its intentional burning contaminates the environment, air, water, and soil, leading to biodiversity loss, bad health, and other problems. Moreover, landfills require specific locations to be able to store waste, while non-biodegradable garbage and chemical waste damage the environment. At the same time, recyclable materials such as papers, metals, plastics are generally mixed with non-recyclable ones at the nearest recycling station, where they should be sorted out manually.

On the other side, selective segregation and recycling of waste materials result in the creation of valuable products from garbage and reduce the negative impact on the environment. For instance, organic waste can be used to generate compost or methane, while other types of trash can go through the recycling process to be reshaped into products. The selective usage of materials and refusal from buying packaged products made of plastic can also help reduce the impact, as well as sort out recyclable materials from those that cannot be recycled. Lastly, innovative technologies applied to waste management will make segregation easier and less laborious, benefiting both civilians and authorities that have to deal with waste management in big cities. Therefore, human activities play a major role in waste management, with a significant impact on how trash is being processed and disposed of.

articles.title: The Ocean’s Invisible Forests: The Power of Phytoplankton
articles.author: Sayam Kala
articles.overview: The tiny drifting organisms behind half of the world’s photosynthesis, the threats they face and how scientists track them.
text: Underneath the beautiful wonder that is the ocean are some things that are rarely thought about by humans. Do you remember learning in class about those little creatures called phytoplankton? Tiny little plankton that float along the surface of the ocean. While small, phytoplankton have a very large impact on the food chain of the ocean. They create food for themselves and other things in the food chain.

Phytoplankton are the forests of the ocean. They are vital parts of the food web and makeup 50% of the world's photosynthesis. Not only do they create oxygen for themselves and other animals, but they also offer food for the smaller creatures in the ocean and even larger ones like fish, birds, and whales. If there weren't plankton in the oceans then our planet wouldn't be able to sustain all of the life that it has.

Unfortunately, in our modern age the amount of plankton in the oceans is hard to predict. There are too many things that can effect on the smallest plankton and make devastating results on the food chain. There exists a growing problem where certain plankton species are blooming due to warmer waters and higher acid levels in the water. Other plankton die because they can't adapt to the new environment.

This causes the animals that used to eat the plankton to have less food than they need and with less numbers of those animals. Not only that, the plankton blooms can make certain parts of the ocean uninhabitable for humans. Certain harmful plankton can make the water surrounding their area toxic and cause inability for healthy seafood. The effects of the changing climates on plankton communities are complex and hard to monitor. However, with the advent of new technology scientists are making progress everyday. For example, researchers can use satellites to calculate chlorophyll in the ocean to predict phytoplankton levels. Scientists also utilize machine learning to better understand the complexities of the environment and its relation to plankton. With both new innovations and traditional methods, researchers are hoping to preserve the plankton and better predict harmful blooms.

articles.title: निसर्ग जपूया, उद्याचा भविष्यकाळ घडवूया
articles.author: Sunny Verma
articles.overview: Protect nature to build tomorrow: everyday habits and collective action that keep the environment in balance.
text: निसर्ग हा केवळ आपल्या सभोवतालचा परिसर नाही, तर मानवी अस्तित्वाचा मूलभूत आधार आहे. स्वच्छ हवा, शुद्ध पाणी, सुपीक माती आणि समृद्ध जैवविविधता यांमुळे पृथ्वीवर जीवन टिकून आहे. मात्र, वाढते शहरीकरण, जंगलतोड, प्लास्टिकचा अतिवापर आणि नैसर्गिक संसाधनांचे अनियंत्रित शोषण यांमुळे पर्यावरणाचा समतोल ढासळत आहे. याचा परिणाम वन्यजीव, मानवी आरोग्य, शेती आणि भावी पिढ्यांवरही होत आहे. हवामानातील बदल, वाढते तापमान आणि पाण्याची टंचाई यांसारख्या समस्यांमुळे पर्यावरण संरक्षणाची गरज अधिक तीव्र झाली आहे.

निसर्गाचे संरक्षण म्हणजे केवळ झाडे लावणे नव्हे, तर पर्यावरणातील प्रत्येक घटकाचे महत्त्व समजून घेणे होय. जंगले कार्बन डायऑक्साइड शोषून हवामानाचे संतुलन राखण्यास मदत करतात. पाणथळ प्रदेश पूरनियंत्रण, भूजल पुनर्भरण आणि अनेक जीवांना अधिवास उपलब्ध करून देतात. मधमाश्या आणि फुलपाखरे यांसारखे परागीभवन करणारे जीव अन्ननिर्मितीत महत्त्वाची भूमिका बजावतात. निसर्गातील सर्व घटक एकमेकांशी जोडलेले असल्यामुळे एका घटकाचे नुकसान संपूर्ण परिसंस्थेवर परिणाम करू शकते. त्यामुळे वनस्पती, प्राणी, पक्षी आणि सूक्ष्मजीव यांचे संरक्षण करणेही तितकेच आवश्यक आहे. पर्यावरण संवर्धनाची सुरुवात आपल्या दैनंदिन सवयींपासून होऊ शकते. पाण्याचा अपव्यय टाळणे, एकदाच वापरल्या जाणाऱ्या प्लास्टिकचा वापर कमी करणे, कचऱ्याचे वर्गीकरण करणे, स्थानिक वृक्षांचे संवर्धन करणे आणि सार्वजनिक वाहतुकीचा वापर वाढवणे ही त्यासाठीची महत्त्वाची पावले आहेत. ओल्या कचऱ्यापासून कंपोस्ट तयार करणे, वस्तूंचा पुनर्वापर करणे आणि शक्य तिथे पर्यावरणपूरक पर्याय निवडणे यांमुळेही प्रदूषण कमी करता येते. विद्यार्थ्यांनी महाविद्यालयीन परिसरात वृक्षगणना, कचरा परीक्षण आणि जैवविविधता निरीक्षण यांसारखे उपक्रम राबवून पर्यावरणाविषयी जागरूकता निर्माण करावी. अशा छोट्या कृतींमधून समाजात मोठा सकारात्मक बदल घडवून आणता येऊ शकतो.

विकास आणि निसर्गसंवर्धन हे एकमेकांच्या विरोधात नसून परस्परांना पूरक असले पाहिजेत. उद्योग, शेती आणि शहरी विकास यांचे नियोजन करताना नैसर्गिक संसाधनांचा जबाबदारीने वापर करणे गरजेचे आहे. शासन, शैक्षणिक संस्था आणि नागरिक यांनी एकत्रितपणे प्रयत्न केल्यास पर्यावरणीय समस्या कमी करण्यासाठी प्रभावी पावले उचलता येतील. प्रत्येकाने निसर्गाप्रती आपली जबाबदारी ओळखून कृती केली, तर अधिक स्वच्छ, हरित आणि संतुलित पर्यावरण निर्माण करणे शक्य होईल. कारण निसर्ग वाचवणे म्हणजे केवळ आजची पृथ्वी जपणे नव्हे, तर उद्याच्या पिढ्यांना जगण्यायोग्य भविष्य देणे होय.

articles.title: Beyond the Watering Can: How Smart Irrigation Uses Sensors
articles.author: Mahak Jain
articles.overview: Soil-moisture sensors and ESP32/Arduino controllers that water crops only when needed, plus the practical limits of the system.
text: Traditional irrigation programs are typically designed on some regular schedule according to which plants are watered regardless of their actual requirements. Smart irrigation wants to solve this problem by using sensors that can evaluate the ground moisture at a certain depth. Thus, they ensure that the grower knows the needs and meet them without any resource being wasted.

The sensors of soil moisture can be capacitive, tensiometers, temperature, rainfall sensors, and so on, which provide the user with the required data in a particular way. Capacitive sensors allow estimating the amount of water contained in the ground in percent based on its electrical properties. In their turn, tensiometers measure the tension of the ground as the roots experience when they drink water. Besides, information on the temperature sensors, rainfall sensors, and the data provided by the local weather forecasts can also be taken into account.
A microcontroller, for example, ESP32 or Arduino, can process the data gained by the sensors and compare it to the desired level of ground moisture.

If the current level is too low, the microcontroller can activate the relay that will open the pump or the solenoid valve to irrigate the field. When the level is sufficient, the process will be stopped. Moreover, such system can have a dashboard that uses which one can visualize the current level and get the notifications on a smartphone.

The described setting may fail due to various reasons, and the most common of them is the incorrect installation or calibration of sensors. The accuracy of the results may vary depending on the properties of the ground, salinity, and the quality of water distribution. In addition, the system may not be worth the money on a small farm due to expensive equipment and the lack of stable internet connections. However, smart irrigation is a great example of how the engineer’s work can benefit society and help achieve sustainability. After all, the amount of water wasted is significant, and its even distribution to the roots of vegetable crops will allow saving this resource.

articles.title: Powering Tomorrow: The Promise of Renewable Energy
articles.author: Arushi Jha
articles.overview: Solar, wind, hydro, geothermal and biomass: the promise of renewables and the challenges of storage, grids and mining.
text: Every day our sun produces unbelievable amounts of energy. It is difficult to believe that men have been using energy sources hidden deep in the Earth for centuries. However, nowadays, due to the increase in demands and global warming, renewable energy sources are seen as a good alternative for the future.

Contrary to coal, oil, and gas, renewable sources of energy are naturally replenished. Examples of those include solar panels, which trap the energy of the sun, wind turbines, which harvest the power of the wind, and hydroelectric plants, which use water power. Other types are geothermal energy derived from the ground and biomass from plants. The use of these sources decreases the impact on the environment and the amount of greenhouse gases when appropriately managed.

Nevertheless, it is not as simple as replacing coal, oil, and gas with renewable energy: for instance, solar and wind energy are not reliable, meaning investments in the batteries and pumped-storage hydroelectric plants. Additionally, the creation of smart grids and accurate predictions will help to equalize the supply-demand of energy and facilitate the transition from one type to another. Undoubtedly, the production of equipment for renewable energy will have negative impacts on the environment as well because it requires mining for materials, so the natural capital and ecosystem approach should be considered as well.

The transition to new energy is socially and economically beneficial as well because it is possible to implement decentralized solar electricity in developing countries to help those who do not have access to electric power. Besides, biomass fuel will decrease indoor air pollution from biomass burning, such as animal dung and firewood. Apart from that, jobs will be created in the renewable energy sector; however, there are many challenges ahead to make these energy sources competitive. In conclusion, it should be said that the development of new energy can be beneficial for our globe if the government and industries invest in the creation of required infrastructure and people change their habits on a small scale.

articles.title: Before The Last Footprint: The Race to Save Vanishing Species
articles.author: Brijesh Gupta
articles.overview: Endangered versus extinct, why every species matters to its ecosystem, and the tools and communities that can still save them.
text: Every species of life has a story that goes back to millions of years. However on every other day many species become extinct and there is nothing that we can do to bring them back. The main difference between the endangered and the extinct species is that the former can be saved while the latter is gone.

Endangerment is the state of animals and plants being at risk of becoming extinct due to various factors such as deforestation, poaching, pollution, changing climates and over hunting. For instance, tigers, Asiatic elephants and gharials are some of the endangered animals that are found in India which is a habitat of many rare species of animals and plants. On the other hand, the extinct species refers to animals and plants that have died out, such as the dodo and the passenger pigeon. Various factors usually lead to the extinction of species, with human activities being the main culprit.

When a species becomes extinct or endangered, not only it is the loss of that specific plant or animal, but also of the functions it played in the community. For example, animals and plants play critical roles in food production, control of other organisms, and overall stability of an ecosystem. The extinction of a species may lead to significant effects in an ecosystem, such as disruption in food production and a decline in the quality of the habitat. Moreover, the indigenous people may lose their ancestral resources, cultural values, and traditions.

The conservation of plants and animals plays a crucial role in sustaining healthy ecosystems that are capable of producing clean food and water, reducing the rate of pollution and climate change, and providing medicinal resources. Some of the measures that can be taken are; restoring and protecting habitats, re-introducing species into the wild, conducting regular surveys, patrols, and researches. Modern technologies such as camera traps and environmental DNA analysis can be used to track and monitor endangered species. Besides technology, the involvement of local people is crucial in the process of conservation as they can provide useful intelligence about the problem.

articles.title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert Shaping Our Future
articles.author: Atharva Hande
articles.overview: The icy continent that holds most of the world’s ice, and why its melting glaciers matter to people everywhere.
text: At the Earth's lowest point lies an oxymoron of a landscape. An icy wasteland surrounded by a turbulent sea but they call it a desert. This desert gets very little precipitation making it the largest desert in the world. Although this barren wasteland may seem desolate, it has a complex ecology whose effects are felt throughout the entire planet.

The vast ice covered desert houses 90% of the worlds ice, and filters 70% of the worlds freshwater. The ice not only helps to sustain the planets ecology, but it also holds off rising sea levels and the surrounding oceans not only absorb heat, but store carbon dioxide. The seasonal ice surrounding Antarctica also helps to pull nutrients into the oceans in order to feed the plants, animals, and even people that call the south polar region home.

Even though it is a remote island continent, the isolated and harsh environment of Antarctica is being affected by human activities. With global warming melting Antarctica's glaciers, rising seas have now swallowed islands and shorelines. The loss of ice also has an effect on the wildlife, because many species depend on the ice in order to survive. But if the entire ice melts, then sea levels will rise even more effecting hundreds of millions of people.

To trace how humans are affecting Antarctica researchers used satellites, unmanned submersibles, and computer modeling. Scientists have to work together to prevent possible disasters and learn more about this unique and vital region.

The isolated continent with the odd name has an equally odd ecosystem. Even though this polar wasteland may seem inhospitable, it still contains life and biodiversity. But these numbers can change as global warming melts the glaciers. The ice on the edge of the world might just be the key to the survival of people on the edges of the world.

articles.title: Green Nanotechnology: Engineering a Cleaner Future
articles.author: Bhoomi Gupta
articles.overview: Nanomaterials that prevent and remove pollution, from photocatalysts to filtration membranes, and the safety checks they need.
text: Pollution control is a long-standing process and is often performed after the damage has occurred. Green nanotechnology was developed to prevent pollution by using nanotechnology to develop materials that would lessen the negative impact on the environment, conserve natural resources and make industrialization more sustainable.

Nanotechnology enables engineering materials to have unique physical properties at the nanometer scale, as a result of an increase in surface area and other properties that are significantly different from what could be expected from a bulk material. For instance, nanomaterials such as titanium dioxide exhibit a photocatalytic activity when exposed to light and can degrade certain organic pollutants when they are introduced into the water. On the other hand, nanotechnology can be used to design novel membranes that are able to remove heavy metals and other toxins from the water and nano-sensors to detect trace amounts of pollutants. Similar approaches can be employed to remove various harmful substances from the environment using nanomaterials.

Aside from removing various pollutants, nanotechnology can be utilized to create new materials and products such as batteries and chemical catalysts that can make the production process more sustainable and conserve natural resources. The use of solar energy, alternative fuels, and other sustainable methods in combination with nanotechnology can greatly reduce the negative impact industrialization has on the environment.

However, nanoparticles and nano-materials might be challenging the environment in unforeseen ways and introducing new substances such as nano-scale materials could have unforeseen consequences. Before introducing such materials into the environment, it is essential to make sure that they are not toxic and can be safely disposed of or recycled. As far as nanotechnology and the environment are concerned, it is vital to ensure that any new materials that have been created are beneficial to the environment and would not introduce new health or environmental hazards.

articles.title: जैविक खेती: मिट्टी की सेहत, भविष्य की सुरक्षा
articles.author: Siddhi Saw
articles.overview: Organic farming as a sustainable path to healthy soil, clean water and food security, with its challenges and solutions.
text: खेती केवल अन्न उत्पादन का माध्यम नहीं, बल्कि मनुष्य और प्रकृति के बीच संतुलन बनाए रखने की एक महत्वपूर्ण कड़ी है। बढ़ती जनसंख्या और खाद्य माँग को पूरा करने के लिए रासायनिक उर्वरकों और कीटनाशकों पर निर्भरता बढ़ी है। हालाँकि, इनके अत्यधिक और असंतुलित उपयोग से मिट्टी की उर्वरता, जल की गुणवत्ता और जैव विविधता पर प्रतिकूल प्रभाव पड़ सकता है। इससे भूमि की प्राकृतिक गुणवत्ता प्रभावित होती है और पारिस्थितिक संतुलन बनाए रखना कठिन हो सकता है। ऐसे में जैविक खेती एक अधिक टिकाऊ विकल्प प्रस्तुत करती है।

जैविक खेती में रासायनिक आदानों पर निर्भर रहने के बजाय प्राकृतिक संसाधनों और जैविक प्रक्रियाओं का उपयोग किया जाता है। गोबर की खाद, वर्मीकम्पोस्ट, हरी खाद और फसल अवशेष मिट्टी में जैविक पदार्थ बढ़ाते हैं, जिससे उसकी संरचना और जल धारण क्षमता में सुधार होता है। फसल चक्र अपनाने, मिश्रित खेती करने तथा नीम आधारित जैव-कीटनाशकों और लाभकारी सूक्ष्मजीवों का उपयोग करने से पोषक तत्त्वों का चक्र संतुलित रखने और कीटों का प्रबंधन करने में सहायता मिलती है। इसके अतिरिक्त, विभिन्न फसलों को उगाने से खेतों में जैव विविधता बढ़ सकती है और मिट्टी के स्वास्थ्य को लंबे समय तक बनाए रखने में मदद मिलती है।

इस पद्धति का महत्व केवल पर्यावरण संरक्षण तक सीमित नहीं है। स्थानीय स्तर पर खाद तैयार करने से कृषि अपशिष्ट का उपयोग होता है, जबकि बाहरी आदानों पर निर्भरता घटने से किसानों को दीर्घकाल में आर्थिक लाभ मिल सकता है। रासायनिक पदार्थों का सीमित उपयोग जल स्रोतों और आसपास के जीवों पर पड़ने वाले प्रतिकूल प्रभावों को कम करने में भी सहायक हो सकता है। फिर भी, जैविक खेती अपनाने में कुछ चुनौतियाँ हैं। शुरुआती वर्षों में उपज घट सकती है, प्रमाणन महँगा हो सकता है और जैविक उत्पादों के लिए उचित बाजार मिलना कठिन हो सकता है। प्रशिक्षण, किसान समूह, स्थानीय खाद निर्माण और वैज्ञानिक मार्गदर्शन इन बाधाओं को कम कर सकते हैं। साथ ही, उपभोक्ताओं में जागरूकता बढ़ाना और किसानों को उचित मूल्य दिलाना भी आवश्यक है।

भविष्य की खेती को केवल अधिक उत्पादन से नहीं, बल्कि मिट्टी, पानी और जैव विविधता को सुरक्षित रखने की क्षमता से भी आँकना होगा। जैविक खेती को सफल बनाने के लिए किसानों, वैज्ञानिकों, सरकार और उपभोक्ताओं के बीच सहयोग आवश्यक है। प्राकृतिक संसाधनों का जिम्मेदारी से उपयोग करके कृषि को अधिक टिकाऊ बनाया जा सकता है। जैविक खेती का वास्तविक उद्देश्य केवल अन्न उगाना नहीं, बल्कि उस धरती को स्वस्थ रखना है, जो आने वाली पीढ़ियों का पेट भरेगी।

articles.title: The Last Drop: A World Thirsting for Water
articles.author: Vikas Madheshiya
articles.overview: The freshwater crisis and how rainwater harvesting, reuse and better policy can stop water from silently running out.
text: Water, one of the things that humans take for granted. We use it, drink it and waste it without a second thought. What happens when the well runs dry? The tap stops dripping? It might be that we don't know what amount we needed potable running water in our day until the day it is gone.

Our ignorance and negligence is causing the current fresh water crisis. The problem is exacerbated by the overuse of ground water and pollution of sources like rivers and lakes leading to shortage of this precious commodity. With unpredictable weather patterns and human-induced climate change, water is becoming a problem that affects all of us. Water is unevenly distributed on planet earth (though it covers most of it ) and only 3% of it is fresh water.

This crisis impacts on every sphere of life, from the farmers whose yields are at stake, to the developing countries which are unable to provide clean drinking water. Loss of aquatic life is a serious concern too since we are losing biodiversity and a food source that has been vital to humankind. It is becoming a socio-economic, political, and now even a survival issue, and it needs to be addressed.

There are various methods that water wastage can be reduced. Harvesting rain water and storing it for later use is a viable option. Treating and reusing water is also effective, apart from using underground reservoirs and other methods like drip irrigation. Water management by the government can lead to policies that prevent water wastage and provide economical and reliable sources of water. Water wastage can be curbed with a concerted effort from government and individuals.

The last drop of water might not be lost on an epic scale, it might sneak away silently and we might not notice till it is too late. It will be when we start to think that this is a resource that will never run out. Our attitude needs to change, and it has to start here and now.

articles.title: When The Earth Loses its Grip: The Silent Crisis of Soil Erosion
articles.author: Vyas Jaiswal
articles.overview: What strips away fertile topsoil, what it costs farms, and the methods that help control erosion.
text: Beneath the surface of every forest, farms, and meadow, there is soil, which is the foundation of the existence of plants and animals. The composition of the soil is formed as a result of the rocks, which it was formed from a long time ago, decomposing. However, the new one can be eroded and taken away by the first gust of wind or rain. The integrity of the top layer of the soil is challenging to restore after its erosion for decades.

Soil erosion is the process of removing and transporting soil. Erosion processes occur due to various reasons, among which destructive human activity,, overgrazed pastures, agriculture, mining, logging, construction, or their combination. The action of the wind, water, or man himself leads to the destruction of the productive layer of the soil, as a result of which it becomes infertile for many years. The consequences of erosion for agriculture can be severe as the lands subject to erosion are vulnerable.

Meanwhile, the consequences of erosion for agriculture can also be expressed in the fact that the soil is increasingly unable to retain moisture, which subsequently negatively affects the farm’s ability to withstand long dry periods. Another short-term consequence of erosion for farms is the decrease in biomass due to the removal of the fertile layer of the soil. Without the elements contained in the surface of the soil, plants cannot develop and grow.

However, to make the consequences of erosion, did not have such a harmful effect on farms, several methods were developed that allow restoring the protective functions of the cover. Thus, such methods as conservation agriculture, crop rotation, contour farming, shaping and maintaining terraces, shelterbelts, and optimal livestock numbers reduce the impact of erosion on the farms. Restoring natural vegetation makes the landscape more resistant to erosion.
It is impossible to stop the process of erosion, but it is possible to prevent and control its consequences. Monitoring and observing erosion changes in the landscape can help assess the risks.

articles.title: Inside the Electric Vehicle: The Code Driving Cleaner Mobility
articles.author: Akansha Verma
articles.overview: Battery management, motor control, regenerative braking and connected software inside a modern electric vehicle.
text: An electric vehicle is more than just a replacement for a petrol powered vehicle, there is an array of sensors and controlllers under the skin which allows it to perform as well as it does. From the battery management system, motors and charging to algorithms which predict the range of the vehicle, software is fundamentally tied to the operation of an electric vehicle.

Under the hood of any electric vehicle lies the battery management system, which ensures that the battery cells are operating within a certain range of parameters. It balances the cells of the battery and aids in maximising the battery's life span whilst ensuring it provides enough power to the motor. The motor controller controls the amount of electricity sent to the motor, allowing the driver to accelerate with the desired amount of power.

Onboard software also makes regenerative braking possible, a feature which allows the vehicle to reclaim some of the energy which would be otherwise lost during braking. The motor, during this process, acts as a generator and charges the battery whilst decelerating. Onboard algorithms also predict the range of the vehicle based on the charge of the battery, and the terrain ahead.

Features like this, as well as vehicle diagnostics and mobile applications tied to the vehicle, require the vehicle to have a connection to the internet. Range predictions require real time data about the road and the weather, and a connection also allows for remote diagnostics and software updates. However, the connection to the internet is also a security risk, and cybersecurity is a growing concern when it comes to connected cars.

Software is, and will continue to be vital to the operation and success of these vehicles. As the technology develops and becomes more mainstream, it will be paramount to utilise software to make operation as smooth and efficient as possible, prolonging the battery life and allowing for a longer range between charges. Sustainability and cleantech is the future, but software is needed to make it happen.

articles.title: When The Water Rises: Understanding the Floods
articles.author: Ritika Gupta
articles.overview: How human activity worsens floods, and how wetlands, resilient cities and early warnings save lives.
text: Floods, one of the most frequent natural disasters, can strip suburbs of their infrastructure and displace thousands of people. While a flood itself is a natural occurrence, it is the humans who usually aggravate the consequences of the disaster.

Downpours, overflows, surpluses, and cloudbursts can trigger a flood, but so can deforestation, construction works done incorrectly, swamp encroachments, impermeable surfaces, and climate change. The complication in forecasting the level of a flood adds up to the challenge in combatting it.

Floods can cause long-standing damage to the local ecosystem, for example, if the water becomes contaminated, it can affect the drinking water supply and destroy agricultural crops. Apart from the damage to the infrastructure, roads, and properties, the residents who survive a flood have to endure the consequences of the disaster. While natural disasters do not discriminate between the rich and the poor, it is the lower-class citizens who are the hardest hit by the aftermath of a flood. However, it has to be noted that a flood does not wash away the nutrient-rich silt, so in that regard, it does not destroy the agricultural potential of the region. In this regard, it is the human activity that leads to disaster and aggravates the consequences of a flood rather than the disaster itself.

Dikes and dams built along with the river banks can offer some protection from the rising waters, but preserving the swamps, forests, and wetlands that act as natural reservoirs is a better preventative measure. It is also a good idea to construct buildings and streets more resiliently and to ensure that the city’s infrastructure is not faulty. Investing more in weather forecasts, cloud monitoring radars, satellites, stream gauges, stream and flood forecasting is paramount. Raising public awareness, engaging the community in disaster risk reduction activities are vital in minimizing the damage caused by a flood, as well as ensuring people’s safety. It is the preparation and warning systems that can make all the difference between people surviving a flood and a large-scale tragedy.

articles.title: सुरक्षिततेची सुरुवात समाजाच्या विचारांतून
articles.author: Aryan Jaiswal
articles.overview: Women’s safety begins with society’s mindset: respect, equality and the courage to stand against injustice.
text: स्त्री-सुरक्षा हा केवळ कायदा आणि सुव्यवस्थेचा प्रश्न नसून समाजाच्या मानसिकतेशी जोडलेला अत्यंत महत्त्वाचा विषय आहे. महिलांच्या संरक्षणासाठी कायदे, हेल्पलाइन आणि कठोर शिक्षेची तरतूद असली, तरी प्रत्यक्ष जीवनात सुरक्षिततेची जाणीव निर्माण होण्यासाठी सामाजिक दृष्टिकोन बदलणे तितकेच आवश्यक आहे. घरापासून सार्वजनिक ठिकाणांपर्यंत स्त्रीला निर्भयपणे वावरण्याचा, स्वतःचे निर्णय घेण्याचा आणि स्वातंत्र्याने जगण्याचा अधिकार मिळणे, हे प्रगत व सुसंस्कृत समाजाचे लक्षण आहे. स्त्री-सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित करणे ही केवळ शासनाची जबाबदारी नसून प्रत्येक नागरिकाचे कर्तव्य आहे.

महिलांच्या सुरक्षिततेसमोरील आव्हाने केवळ छेडछाड किंवा हिंसाचारापुरती मर्यादित नाहीत. कामाच्या ठिकाणी होणारा भेदभाव, ऑनलाइन छळ, पाठलाग, संमतीकडे दुर्लक्ष आणि पीडितेलाच दोष देण्याची प्रवृत्ती यांमुळेही असुरक्षिततेचे वातावरण निर्माण होते. अनेकदा एखादी घटना घडल्यानंतर तिच्यावर चर्चा होते; मात्र अशा घटनांना कारणीभूत ठरणाऱ्या पूर्वग्रहांवर, चुकीच्या समजुतींवर आणि वर्तनावर पुरेसे लक्ष दिले जात नाही. मुलगा आणि मुलगी यांच्यात भेद न करता परस्पर आदर, समानता आणि संमतीचे महत्त्व लहानपणापासून शिकवणे गरजेचे आहे. कुटुंब, शाळा आणि समाज यांनी एकत्रितपणे ही मूल्ये रुजवली, तर पुढील पिढीत अधिक संवेदनशील आणि जबाबदार दृष्टिकोन विकसित होऊ शकतो.

यासाठी प्रत्येक नागरिकाची भूमिका महत्त्वाची आहे. सार्वजनिक ठिकाणी गैरवर्तन दिसल्यास सुरक्षितपणे हस्तक्षेप करणे, पीडित व्यक्तीला दोष न देता तिचे म्हणणे ऐकून घेणे, ऑनलाइन छळाची तक्रार करण्यास मदत करणे आणि मुलांना जबाबदार वर्तनाची जाणीव करून देणे, ही कृतीतून व्यक्त होणारी सामाजिक जबाबदारी आहे. शैक्षणिक संस्थांनी लैंगिक संवेदनशीलतेविषयी जागरूकता निर्माण करावी, तर कार्यस्थळांनी तक्रार निवारणाची प्रभावी आणि विश्वासार्ह यंत्रणा उपलब्ध करून द्यावी. महिलांना त्यांच्या हक्कांची माहिती देणे, आवश्यक मदत सहज उपलब्ध करून देणे आणि तक्रार करणाऱ्या व्यक्तीला सुरक्षित वातावरण मिळवून देणेही तितकेच महत्त्वाचे आहे.

कायद्याची भीती गुन्हे रोखण्यास मदत करू शकते; परंतु आदराची भावना, समानतेची जाणीव आणि अन्यायाविरुद्ध उभे राहण्याची तयारी सुरक्षित संस्कृती घडवते. स्त्री-सुरक्षेची जबाबदारी केवळ महिलांनी स्वतःचे संरक्षण करण्यापुरती मर्यादित ठेवता कामा नये. महिलांच्या स्वातंत्र्यावर बंधने घालण्याऐवजी समाजाने त्यांना समान संधी, सन्मान आणि सुरक्षित वातावरण उपलब्ध करून देण्यावर भर दिला पाहिजे. सुरक्षित समाजाची निर्मिती केवळ नियमांमुळे होत नाही, तर प्रत्येक व्यक्तीच्या विचारांत आणि कृतीतून ती साकार होते. ज्या समाजात स्त्रीच्या स्वातंत्र्याचा आदर केला जातो आणि अन्यायाविरुद्ध प्रत्येक जण उभा राहतो, तिथेच खरी सुरक्षितता रुजते.

articles.title: Rooted in Healing: The Hidden Science of Medicinal Plants
articles.author: Satyam Gupta
articles.overview: Traditional herbal knowledge meets modern science, and why medicinal plants must be studied, protected and used carefully.
text: Long, ago before the appearance of pharmacies on street corners, people were using various parts of plants to cure different diseases. The information, as well as the experience of healing has been passed from generation to generation, and over a long period of time has contributed to the development of medicine. Today, scientists are also interested in herbal medicine since it plays an important role in the history of science, literature, and medicine.

Herbal medicine has a vast repository of useful substances for fighting pathogens, parasites, and other invaders. In fact, the active ingredients of many drugs were originally isolated from plants. For scientists, plant drugs are of particular interest since they have promising prospects for medicine. However, despite the long history of healing properties, drugs derived from plants require more rigorous study and preparation.

Unfortunately, in the global sense, medicinal plants are not always safe or effective. Although they can contain many useful substances, improper preparation, incorrect dose, interaction with other drugs, and lack of knowledge of contraindications can be dangerous for the human health. Today, medicinal plants play a big role in the healthcare system of many countries since they are often the only option when the opportunity for the conventional therapy is limited. Nevertheless, herbal medicine needs to be supported not only by tradition but also by science.

In addition, the development and use of medicinal plants require protection and preservation of natural heritage. Local ecosystems, in which flora develops, must be preserved; otherwise, there will be no raw materials for drug production.

Finally, medicinal plants connect people’s knowledge and experience with innovation and progress. A huge number of plant species that are useful for humans and the environment should be preserved for future generations. These treasures of nature have to develop and benefit of humankind. However, they need to be studied, protected, and used properly.

articles.title: Sunlight Under Surveillance: The Engineering Behind Solar Power
articles.author: Aditya Jha
articles.overview: Inverters, MPPT, sensors and IoT monitoring that keep a solar PV system efficient and catch faults early.
text: Solar technology comprises photovoltaic (PV) panels that generate electricity. Solar PV advanced systems have sensors, control electronics, power converters and software that assist in electricity production, diagnosing malfunction and optimizing the electricity production.

In the PV system, semiconductor cells allow the conversion of sunlight into direct current (DC). Inverters then change DC into alternating current (AC) that is suitable to power homes and businesses. A maximum power point tracker (MPPT) ensures that the direct current from solar panels is manipulated into an alternating current.

Sensors enable the tracking of the performance of a solar PV installation. Irradiance sensors measure solar power while temperature sensors monitor temperatures of panels, inverters, and other equipment. Current and voltage sensors record the amount of current generated by the PV system.

The sensors in a solar PV system can be connected to data loggers or internet of things (IoT) platform which stores the information in the cloud. The software then uses the data to compare the electricity being produced and issues alerts in case of a malfunction. For instance, solar irradiance sensors can track the amount of electricity that is expected to be produced. If the panels are generating less electricity than expected, there is a malfunction that may need investigation. The malfunctions range from shading of the panels, dirty panels, faults in the inverter, and wiring problems. Some solar PV systems are intelligent and use artificial intelligence (AI) to predict the time to carry out maintenance and recommend the best solar technologies to a homeowner. Cleaning robots can also be used to keep the panels clean while solar trackers can be utilized to follow the sun. However, these technologies may require more energy, cost, and maintenance to add to their worth.

In a solar PV system with batteries, the battery management system monitors the charge and health of the battery. Combined with smart inverters, they regulate the electricity from the solar panels, battery, and the utility to meet the loads in the home or business.

articles.title: Where Land Meets The Sea: The Living Shield of Mangroves
articles.author: Amit Bhagat
articles.overview: Mangroves as coastal shields and carbon sinks, and the development and sea-level threats they face.
text: At the boundary between continents and oceans, where there are tides, there is a habitat called mangroves. The plants of this habitat have adapted to the extreme conditions in the intertidal zone and have some unique life functions. Mangroves are not so well known, as they are very productive ecosystems, a valuable food resource for wildlife.

Mangroves are found in the tropical and subtropical latitudes, between 25°N and 25°S. They flourish in the intertidal mudflat areas, where many plants cannot survive due to the high salt content in the soil. However, mangroves have unique adaptations that allow them to accumulate salt or resist its harmful effects. Firstly, the root systems of mangrove trees filter some salt from the water and hold the trees together, resisting the force of the tides. The mangroves prop roots trap sediments and organic matter that provide food for many aquatic species. Secondly, mangroves’ vegetation is thick enough to filter large water bodies, protecting coast settlements from the force of waves and the storms. Moreover, the mangrove forests are a carbon sink, soaking up carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, lowering its harmful effect on the environment.

Unfortunately, today mangrove forests are threatened to disappear as people often want to develop coastal areas for industrial or agricultural purposes. Besides, global warming leads to increased erosion and altered estuarine hydrology, disrupting the breeding of many species. Another threat is the increasing level of the sea; mangroves cannot move their location inland to higher ground because human-made objects block their way. Thus, the loss of this unique ecosystem will result in a reduction of carbon sinks, decreased fisheries, and loss of protection from waves and storm surges. Thus, the protection and restoration of mangrove forests should be a priority for coastal states.

articles.title: Green Invasion: When a Beautiful Bloom Chokes Our Waterways
articles.author: Sanmay Chavan
articles.overview: Water hyacinth, a beautiful invader that chokes wetlands, and the manual, biological and biogas-based ways to control it.
text: Water hyacinth is a free floating perennial aquatic plant. That is native to South America. The plant belongs to the world's aggressive invasive species with adverse effects on the environment. Water hyacinth is an invasive plant introduced deliberately that has overtaken the wetlands.

Water hyacinth grows aggressively under suitable conditions, choking the waterways and preventing light penetration into other plants. When the plants die, their decay process removes the oxygen in the water, killing other organisms. Water hyacinth can cause catastrophic damage to the wetland ecosystem because of its ability to engulf the waterways by choking them. The plants can also make fishing challenging and navigate water difficult. In addition, water hyacinth can lead to the loss of agricultural produce, affecting the farmer's income. The leaves of the plants can retain stagnant water that can be a breeding ground for disease-bearing mosquitoes. Controlling the invasive species can be a daunting task. The water hyacinth plants can be pulled from the water and surrounding wetlands manually. However, it is essential to ensure that they are not re-invaded, and other potential food sources are limited. The plants can be controlled alternatively using alternative measures such as using biocontrol agents to manage their infestation. The manual gathering of the plant can be coupled with the use of weevils that parasitize the plants and reduce their spread. The plants can then be burned, composted, or used to generate biogas depending on their level of contamination. The leaves can also be shredded and added to biogas digesters or composted. Scientists are also considering other strategies for destroying the plants, including exploring other uses of the plant that will prevent their growth in the wetlands.

Water hyacinth teaches humans a lesson regarding the local biome. Based on the description of the plant, one would have thought that it was a beneficial addition to the wetland because of its beauty. However, little did the people know that it would destroy the wetlands, leaving them with wastelands with little or no agricultural activity.

articles.title: डिजिटल खाई से ज्ञान के सेतु तक: ग्रामीण शिक्षा की नई राह
articles.author: Rehan Khan
articles.overview: Bridging the digital divide so rural students get equal access to quality learning.
text: शिक्षा किसी भी समाज की प्रगति की नींव है, लेकिन इसकी गुणवत्ता और उपलब्धता आज भी हर विद्यार्थी के लिए समान नहीं है। शहरों में स्मार्ट कक्षाओं, इंटरनेट और ऑनलाइन अध्ययन सामग्री के माध्यम से सीखने के नए अवसर विकसित हो रहे हैं, जबकि अनेक ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में विद्यार्थी बिजली की अनियमित आपूर्ति, कमजोर नेटवर्क और डिजिटल उपकरणों की कमी से जूझ रहे हैं। यह अंतर केवल तकनीकी सुविधाओं का नहीं, बल्कि अवसरों और भविष्य की संभावनाओं का भी है। ऐसी परिस्थितियों में ग्रामीण विद्यार्थियों को समान शैक्षणिक अवसर उपलब्ध कराना आवश्यक हो जाता है।

डिजिटल शिक्षा ग्रामीण विद्यार्थियों के लिए ज्ञान की दुनिया के द्वार खोल सकती है। ऑनलाइन व्याख्यान, ई-पुस्तकें, आभासी प्रयोगशालाएँ और शैक्षणिक मंच उन्हें विद्यालय की पाठ्यपुस्तकों से आगे सीखने का अवसर देते हैं। दीक्षा (DIKSHA) जैसे मंचों पर उपलब्ध डिजिटल सामग्री इस दिशा में उपयोगी है। विद्यार्थी अपनी सुविधानुसार विषयों को दोहरा सकते हैं और कठिन अवधारणाओं को बेहतर ढंग से समझ सकते हैं। फिर भी, स्मार्टफोन या इंटरनेट की उपलब्धता मात्र से गुणवत्तापूर्ण शिक्षा सुनिश्चित नहीं होती। साझा मोबाइल, महँगा डेटा, स्थानीय भाषा में सामग्री की कमी और डिजिटल कौशल का अभाव विद्यार्थियों की सीखने की प्रक्रिया को प्रभावित कर सकते हैं।

इस चुनौती से निपटने के लिए प्रत्येक विद्यालय में डिजिटल अध्ययन केंद्र, ऑफलाइन उपलब्ध शैक्षणिक सामग्री और सौरऊर्जा से संचालित उपकरण विकसित किए जा सकते हैं। शिक्षकों को तकनीकी प्रशिक्षण देना तथा स्थानीय भाषाओं में संवादात्मक पाठ तैयार करना भी आवश्यक है। महाविद्यालयों के विद्यार्थी स्वयंसेवक बनकर ग्रामीण बच्चों को डिजिटल साक्षरता सिखा सकते हैं। पुस्तकालयों और सामुदायिक केंद्रों में इंटरनेट तथा कंप्यूटर की सुविधा उपलब्ध कराने से भी विद्यार्थियों को लाभ मिल सकता है। इस प्रकार तकनीक, सामुदायिक भागीदारी और पारंपरिक शिक्षण का समन्वय अधिक प्रभावी परिणाम दे सकता है।

ग्रामीण विद्यार्थियों में प्रतिभा की कमी नहीं, बल्कि कई बार अवसरों की कमी होती है। सही मार्गदर्शन, उपयुक्त संसाधन और सीखने के अनुकूल वातावरण मिलने पर वे भी अपनी क्षमताओं का पूरा विकास कर सकते हैं। डिजिटल सुविधाओं का उद्देश्य केवल शिक्षा को आधुनिक बनाना नहीं, बल्कि उसे अधिक सुलभ, समावेशी और न्यायसंगत बनाना होना चाहिए। जब तकनीक गाँव की अंतिम कक्षा तक पहुँचेगी, तभी शिक्षा का प्रकाश हर भविष्य को समान रूप से रोशन कर सकेगा।

articles.title: How AI Turns Climate Data into Early Warnings
articles.author: Anuj Chaudhary
articles.overview: Using AI to find patterns in climate data and warn communities about cyclones, droughts and heatwaves in time.
text: Every shifting wind, warmer temperature, and shifting ocean current give us whispers of what our future holds. And with the aid of the powerful tool that is Artificial Intelligence (AI), we can utilise what power those whispers have to help us decipher the ever-elusive mass of climate data that will help provide us with an early-warning system of sorts to help us prepare the Earth for coming challenges.
While just using data to predict the future is already very valuable, the power to identify patterns in visual information, observations, and measurements in something AI is especially good at.

Those patterns can then be used to predict everything from rainfall to cyclone formation, as well as help predict the consequences such as droughts and heatwaves. This information can then be used by scientists and the media alike to help inform the public on an incoming natural disaster, helping keep them safe.

The same information can help farmers identify dry periods where they will need to water their plants, or even allow us to formulate an evacuation plan for the region in the path of a particularly dangerous cyclone. We could even use this to help cities prepare for severe heatwaves, helping set up emergency coolant stations for people who don't have access to airconditioning to help them survive.

Of course, there is a limit to how much we can predict, as it takes a long time to gather and verify information, and even longer to prepare and test it. The power of AI to predict and prepare is an interesting prospect, one that has the potential to give us the power of preparation for the climate crisis before it leaves us too little time to do anything at all.

poems.title: The Last Lesson
poems.author: Ankita Jha
poems.summary: A farewell to the classroom, and the lesson in kindness that outlives it.
stanzas: The final bell rang softly through the air,
The sunlight settled gently on each chair;
The board still held the words we used to know,
While evening taught the class to let things go.
We thought that learning lived in ink and lines,
In dates remembered, facts, and strict designs;
Yet one last question made us pause and see:
What use is knowledge if we cease to be
Kind to the world, and all that we may see?
Our teacher smiled, then quietly withdrew,
Leaving behind more than the words we knew;
A lesson in courage, a choice to care,
A seed of hope that all of us could share.
We learnt that truth may challenge what is right,
That silent wrongs grow stronger out of sight;
That progress means not merely reaching high,
But lifting those the world has passed by.
And years from now, when these old halls are gone,
When new dreams rise and other bells ring on,
We'll know the lesson time could never erase:
We leave the classroom, but not what it gave.

poems.title: The Tide That Took Truth
poems.author: Gaurang Bhoir
poems.summary: The sea remembers what we throw away — a plea for cleaner rivers and restored reefs.
stanzas: The moon drew silver on the restless sea,
While waves rehearsed what no one wished to hear;
The shore held secrets buried silently,
And washed-up plastic whispered year by year.
The coral gardens paled beneath the blue,
Where once a thousand colours danced in light;
The nets came back with nothing but the few,
And vanished reefs dissolved into the night.
The river brought the city’s sins downstream,
Each bottle, stain, and chemical disguise;
We called the water clear, a harmless dream,
While truth lay choking where the current dies.
Yet every tide returns what we discard,
Each broken shell, each scar the waters keep;
The sea remembers, though we turn our guard,
And bears our careless history in its deep.
So let the waves no longer plead in vain,
Let cleaner rivers meet the ocean’s door;
Restore the reefs, let life return again,
And leave no hidden wound beneath the shore.

poems.title: Black and White
poems.author: Chaitanya Sawant
poems.summary: A child’s question that breaks the frames of prejudice: see the person, not the hue.
stanzas: They drew their lines in black and white,
And taught the world whom to embrace;
They turned a shade into a right,
And made a boundary out of face.
A child once asked, “What makes us stray,
When all our hearts beat just the same?
Why does the world look first at grey,
And judge a soul before its name?”
Some doors swing wide, some doors stay closed,
Some dreams are buried before they rise;
While prejudice, in silence, grows,
Behind the mask of judging eyes.
But skin cannot measure what we know,
Nor shade determine what we do;
No colour tells how hearts can grow,
Or makes one life worth more than two.
So let us break the frames we made,
And see the person, not the hue;
For no true dawn has ever stayed
In a world that sees in just two views.

poems.title: The Fading Fall
poems.author: Riya Raut
poems.summary: Autumn’s quiet lesson in grace, and the peace found in letting go.
stanzas: The amber leaves descend without a sound,
Like golden letters drifting through the air;
While autumn paints the earth in shades profound,
And scatters russet beauty everywhere.
The branches sway beneath the mellow skies,
As gentle breezes stir the fading gold;
The sun sinks softly where the horizon lies,
And twilight wraps the fields in shades of old.
The birds prepare to leave their leafy home,
Their distant calls grow faint across the blue;
While fallen leaves along the pathways roam,
And morning veils the grass with silver dew.
The forest wears a crown of copper light,
As crimson mingles with the fading green;
Each leaf that falls makes way for autumn’s night,
A quiet farewell to the summer scene.
And though the golden days must fade away,
Their beauty lingers in the heart and mind;
For autumn teaches, in its own sweet way,
That grace and peace in letting go we find.

poems.title: मोहोरातली कुहू
poems.author: Bhavan Jha
poems.summary: The koel’s song in mango blossom, and a call to protect the trees and birds that carry it.
stanzas: आंब्याच्या मोहोरात दरवळे, गंध सोनेरी पहाटेचा,
पानोपानी सूर झुलविते, स्वर कोकिळेच्या गाण्याचा।
कुहू कुहूच्या नादामधुनी, रान जागते हळुवार,
वाऱ्याच्या मंद झुळुकेवर, डोलतो हिरवा संसार।
नभात निळाई, उन्हात कोवळीक, फांदीवरती गोड तान,
फुलाफुलांतून अलगद उमटे, ऋतुराजाचा नवा गान।
मोहोराच्या त्या सुगंधात, आठवणींचे झरे वाहती,
कोकिळेच्या एका सुराने, मनात वसंतफुले फुलती।
पण कुठे हरवली हिरवाई, कुठे थांबला रानवारा?
काँक्रीटच्या या गर्दीत आता, विरळ होतसे पक्ष्यांचे थवे सारे।
झाडे तोडून वाटा रुंदावल्या, हरवली घरट्यांची छाया,
मोहोर उरेल का उद्याला, जर नसेल फांदीची माया?
लावू रोपे, जपूया राने, पाणवठ्यांना देऊ जीवन,
पक्ष्यांसाठी राखू थोडे, आभाळ, झाडे अन् अंगण।
उद्याच्या लेकरांना ऐकू दे, तोच कोकिळेचा मधुर स्वर,
मोहोरातली कुहू निनादो, युगानुयुगे अविरत सुंदर।

poems.title: Before the Green Fades
poems.author: Vanshika Shrivastav
poems.summary: Before the last bird leaves the tree: a call to plant, restore and protect.
stanzas: Before the green fades from the hills,
Before the last bird leaves the tree,
Before the stream forgets its thrills,
Let earth reclaim what once was free.
The forests keep what we forget,
The footprints pressed in wounded ground;
Each fallen tree, each drying wetland,
Leaves silence where life once resounded.
We build our towers, pave our way,
And call the changing skyline grace;
Yet who will teach the dawn to stay,
When concrete takes the wild’s own place?
A seed still sleeps beneath the stone,
A river waits beyond the dam;
The earth can heal, but not alone
Hope needs more hands than words can span.
So plant the shade our children need,
Let rivers run both clear and wide;
Choose less, restore, protect, and seed
There’s still a world before the green has died.

poems.title: Voices Unbound
poems.author: Sanskriti Prasad
poems.summary: On the courage to speak, and a world transformed by every word.
stanzas: Behind closed doors, where silence learns to stay,
Lie words that fear the light of break of day;
Each unheard thought, each dream denied its flight,
Waits for a voice to turn the dark to light.
A voice may tremble, falter, break, or bend,
Yet carry truths that silence cannot mend;
For change begins when one dares to speak,
And finds the strength the world calls weak.
Not every voice is heard within the crowd,
Not every truth is welcomed when said loud;
Some speak through art, some through a written line,
Some rise through acts that make the world more kind.
Let no one's language, birth, or name decide
Which dreams may bloom and which must hide;
For minds grow richer when perspectives meet,
And justice starts where listening is complete.
So let our voices travel far and wide,
Like rivers breaking through the walls that divide;
For freedom is not merely being heard,
It is a world transformed by every word.

poems.title: बूँदों का सफ़र
poems.author: Adarsh Pandey
poems.summary: The journey of a raindrop from cloud to sea, and why every drop deserves respect.
stanzas: बादल की पलकों से उतरी, बूँद चली अनजान डगर,
लेकर सपनों की नमी, धरती की ओर उसका सफ़र।
पत्तों पर मोती बन चमकी, फूलों से कुछ बात कही,
सूखी मिट्टी की साँसों में, उसने नई सौगात भरी।
कभी नदी की बाँहों में, कभी सागर के विस्तार में,
कभी हिमशिखरों की चुप्पी में, कभी खेतों की पुकार में।
पत्थर काटे, राहें मोड़ीं, फिर भी चलती रही निरंतर,
एक बूँद में छिपा हुआ था, जीवन का सारा समंदर।
पर शहरों की भागदौड़ में, उसका मोल भुलाया गया,
नल से बहते अनमोल जल को, यूँ ही व्यर्थ बहाया गया।
सूखे कुएँ, उदास तलैया, प्यासे पंछी, तपता वन,
बूँद ने पूछा—“मेरे बिन क्या, मुस्काएगा यह जीवन?”
आओ, इसकी राह सँवारें, हर बूँद का सम्मान करें,
वर्षा-जल को थाम के रखें, नदियों का कल्याण करें।
आज बचाएँगे जो पानी, कल का हर आँगन हँसेगा,
बूँद-बूँद से जीवन फूटेगा, धरती का आँचल फिर खिलेगा।
न बादल का सफ़र है छोटा, न जीवन की डोर क्षणिक,
जल की हर बूँद में बसती, आशा की धड़कन शाश्वत।
जब तक धरती, जब तक अम्बर, इसका रिश्ता रहे अमर,
हर बूँद की रक्षा में ही, सुरक्षित है कल का सफ़र।

projects.name: Bhajan Sandhya
projects.desc: Thirty-eight TCET NSS volunteers joined the University of Mumbai NSS Unit at the Gateway of India for an evening of devotional and patriotic bhajans marking Gandhi Jayanti and the International Day of Non-Violence.
projects.quote: In a gentle way, you can shake the world and inspire lasting change in humanity.
text: The Bhajan Sandhya programme was held at Mumbai’s Gateway of India on 2nd October 2026, commemorating Mahatma Gandhi’s birth anniversary and the International Day of Non-Violence. The event aimed to promote peace, unity, and harmony through collective prayer and devotional songs, encouraging participants to embrace Gandhian values and foster mutual respect, understanding, and peaceful coexistence within society for a better tomorrow.

Organized by the University of Mumbai NSS Unit, the Bhajan Sandhya created a serene atmosphere through patriotic and devotional bhajans. Thirty-eight TCET NSS volunteers attended to honour Mahatma Gandhi’s birth anniversary and observe the International Day of Non-Violence, promoting peace, unity and collective reflection.

Amidst the iconic backdrop of the Gateway of India, the evening's collective prayers and devotional music reinforced timeless teachings of peace and communal harmony. Dignitaries and university officials praised the volunteers for their exemplary discipline, active involvement, and dedication to national service. Participating in such a prestigious venue allowed the students to connect with peers from across the city, fostering a profound sense of camaraderie. Ultimately, the programme successfully inspired the youth to internalize Gandhian ideals and carry the message of non-violence forward into their daily lives and future community initiatives, promoting unity, compassion, and social responsibility.

projects.name: Tree Plantation Drive
projects.desc: 30 volunteers planted 60 saplings, including guava, chikoo and flowering varieties, at INS Hamla under the national “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” campaign.
projects.quote: He who plants a tree, plants a hope that grows for generations to come.
text: The TCET NSS UNIT organized a Tree Plantation Drive on 18th July 2026 at INS Hamla, located on Marve Road, Malad (West), Mumbai. 30 volunteers actively participated in this environmental initiative, promoting the national “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” campaign and spreading awareness about environmental conservation, ecological responsibility, and the importance of protecting nature for future generations. Their efforts encouraged sustainable practices and inspired collective action.

The TCET NSS UNIT organized a Tree Plantation Drive at INS Hamla, Marve, promoting environmental preservation and social responsibility. Volunteers planted 60 saplings, including guava, chikoo, and flowering varieties, encouraging biodiversity and ecological sustainability through community participation.

Sustainable green cover and ecological restoration were promoted through active groundwork, encouraging students and personnel to support the nationwide campaign and dedicate a sapling in honor of their mothers. NSS volunteers helped coordinate the activity, dig pits, plant and water the saplings, interact with base officials, and create awareness about the importance of afforestation and community participation. The drive connected the values of nature conservation with the spirit of social service. The drive encouraged students to support the participating defense and environmental organizations and appreciate the dedication and efforts involved in nurturing young trees.

projects.name: Medical Survey
projects.desc: A door-to-door health survey at Singh Estate assessing stale water, mosquito-breeding risks and household disease history, while raising awareness about water-borne diseases.
projects.quote: Prevention is better than cure, as early care protects health and saves lives.
text: Organized by the TCET NSS UNIT at Singh Estate on 25th July 2026, the medical survey involved volunteers collecting health data from local residents. It aimed to understand community health preferences, raise awareness about water-borne diseases, and enable volunteers to interact with local families while gathering crucial information about prevailing health concerns, supporting better healthcare planning and promoting preventive measures for improved community well-being.

The objective of the initiative was to assess stale water accumulation, mosquito-breeding risks, and household disease history while promoting preventive healthcare. The volunteers focused on identifying environmental hazards and enquiring every household about recent and/or current disease history.

Beyond routine data collection, the initiative played a crucial role in analyzing the ratio of residents leaning toward private healthcare services versus those relying on government facilities. By engaging directly and empathetically with community members on a door-to-door basis, the dedicated team successfully raised vital awareness regarding the prevention of vector and water-borne seasonal disease outbreaks. The volunteers distributed practical informational guidance on maintaining proper personal hygiene and adopting safe water storage practices, ultimately working to safeguard public health and build long-term resilience in the area, ensuring healthier communities through awareness and prevention.

projects.name: Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan
projects.desc: A University of Mumbai initiative educating students about the harmful effects of substance abuse and the role of youth in building an addiction-free society.
projects.quote: Break the chains of addiction, unlock the doors to freedom.
text: The University of Mumbai organized Nasha Mukti Abhiyan on 30th July 2026 to raise awareness about the harmful effects of substance abuse and promote the vision of a drug-free India. The initiative aimed to educate students about the importance of prevention, responsible decision-making, and healthy living. It emphasized the role of youth in combating addiction and encouraged collective efforts to build a healthier, safer, and addiction-free society.

The initiative focused on educating students about the harmful effects of drug addiction on physical health, mental well-being, families, and society. Through awareness and meaningful discussions, participants were encouraged to understand the importance of prevention, make responsible decisions, and support individuals affected by substance abuse. The programme highlighted the role of youth in building a healthier and safer society. The Honorable speaker addressed the gathering and highlighted the importance of achieving a drug-free India. The session provided valuable information about substance abuse, its consequences, and preventive measures. It encouraged students to recognize the significance of awareness, develop healthy habits, and discourage substance use among their peers. projects.name: CPR Training
projects.desc: Experts from Holy Family Multispeciality Hospital, Bandra trained 90+ participants in recognising cardiac arrest and performing CPR on medical dummies.
projects.quote: Every second counts when life is on the line, and timely action saves precious lives.
text: Attended by volunteers alongside esteemed faculty members on 9th October 2026, this specialized cardiac arrest awareness training session successfully equipped all participants with vital, life-saving skills. Attendees were carefully guided through comprehensive educational videos that clearly and vividly demonstrated how to promptly recognize the early warning signs and symptoms of a sudden cardiac arrest, enabling them to take immediate and effective action during high-stress scenarios.

The TCET NSS UNIT organized an impactful cardiac arrest awareness training session where experts from Holy Family Multispeciality Hospital, Bandra, provided immersive, practical hands-on dummy training and detailed instructional videos focused on accurately identifying and responding to critical medical emergencies.

Following the visual instructions, participants received invaluable, direct practical training using specialized medical dummies to master proper chest compression techniques, cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) rhythms, and standard emergency response protocols. This immersive, real-world exposure instilled profound confidence in everyone present, ensuring they are thoroughly prepared to handle critical medical crises effectively before professional emergency medical services arrive on the scene. The initiative bridged the crucial gap between theoretical awareness and practical readiness and empowered both students and faculty with essential knowledge and life-saving capabilities.
